subject: Technical runbook proposal: rate limiting & idempotency for Acme Health integration
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Technical runbook proposal: rate limiting & idempotency for Acme Health integration

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the reliability/throughput questions you flagged: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Integration surfaces: SDK auth (API keys / optional mTLS), routing by region, structured output + tool calling for your downstream systems, and an embeddings + reranker flow for semantic search.
- Non-functional asks: predictable latency under bursty traffic, clear guidance on 429 handling and idempotency, and an approach for per-tenant quotas.

What I'm proposing next (technical runbook we can iterate on):
1) SDK & auth checklist (what to configure in your dev/stage/prod environments, recommended headers).
2) Request routing: primary region + cross-region fallback and how we degrade gracefully.
3) Embeddings + reranker pattern: batching guidance, cold cache warm-up, and expected token/unit costs.
4) Rate limit & retry policy: token-bucket quotas, burst sizing, 429 semantics, Retry-After handling, exponential backoff + jitter, and mandatory Idempotency-Key usage for mutating calls.
5) Ops/runbook artifacts: log keys to surface (request_id, model, route), alert thresholds, and a postmortem template.

Attached is a first-pass runbook (redwood_runbook_v1.pdf) and the demo recording. Can you confirm: peak sustained QPS, expected burst patterns (duration/frequency), and whether the EU region is required for this phase? Once I have that, Jonas will draft concrete rate-limit numbers and a config snippet your SREs can drop into their ingress policy.

Proposed next step: 30m technical sync (engineers + SRE) — I included a tentative time in the follow-up.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical runbook proposal: rate limiting & idempotency for Acme Health integration

Thanks Vanessa — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side that will shape the runbook: 

Traffic profile:
- Peak sustained QPS: ~120 r/s for our primary inference endpoint.
- Short bursts: up to ~300 r/s for 2–3 minutes during morning syncs and nightly batch jobs. Bursts are infrequent (2–3x/day).

Embeddings/reranker usage:
- Embedding batches are typically 32–128 vectors. Reranking happens for ~15% of queries and is latency-sensitive (target <= 180ms p95).

Compliance/regional requirement:
- For PHI-sensitive workloads we'll need US region only for now; EU may come later.

Questions for your engineers:
1) Do you support an Idempotency-Key or equivalent header on generation requests? Particularly for any reranker / multi-step pipeline we might want dedupe behavior.
2) On 429 responses: do you return Retry-After header and a standardized error body? We want client-side retry rules to be deterministic.

I attached a short note from our SREs with sample ingress limits. If you can incorporate that into the runbook that would help.

— Alex
Alex Moreno, Staff Architect
Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_sre_ingress_limits.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@acmehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical runbook proposal: rate limiting & idempotency for Acme Health integration

Alex — thanks for the detail. A few concrete proposals and what we can ship in the SDK/runbook tomorrow: 

1) Quota model & burst handling\- Per-tenant token-bucket enforced at the edge with two parameters: steady_rate (tokens/sec) and burst_capacity (max tokens). Suggested starting numbers for your profile: steady_rate=120, burst_capacity=320 (allows short 300 r/s bursts for ~10s without dropping). We'll tune after a week of telemetry.

2) 429 semantics & Retry-After\- Our platform returns 429 with a Retry-After (seconds) when we can compute a precise retry window. For transient capacity rejections we return 429 + Retry-After. For global throttles we also include a structured JSON body: {"error":"quota_exceeded","recommended_backoff_ms":<n>}. (SDKs parse both headers and body.)

3) Retry strategy (recommended)\- Use exponential backoff with full jitter (per 'Exponential Backoff and Jitter' best practices):
  - initial_delay = 200–500ms (configurable)
  - factor = 2.0; max_delay = 10000ms
  - attempts = 5 by default for idempotent calls; mutable/streaming requests require explicit client-side handling.

4) Idempotency and request identifiers\- For any non-idempotent multi-step operations (e.g., job creation, reranker index builds) require a client-supplied Idempotency-Key (we accept X-Idempotency-Key or Idempotency-Key). For per-request telemetry and debugging we recommend also supplying X-Request-ID (UUID). Our logs index on both fields.

5) SDK options we will include in the runbook (text example included in attachment rate_limit_config_examples.txt):
  - auto_retry.enabled = true
  - auto_retry.max_attempts = 5
  - backoff.initial_ms = 300
  - backoff.max_ms = 10000
  - headers: ["X-Request-ID", "Idempotency-Key"]
  - batch.embeddings.max_batch = 128

6) Structured output & tool calling notes\- Streaming completions can be resumed by streaming tokens and using resume cursors in metadata; for deterministic reranking we recommend returning a stable item id in the model output so downstream can reconcile results after retries.

I've attached a short runbook fragment with examples (rate_limit_config_examples.txt). Happy to convert to YAML/JSON for your ops if that helps.

— Jonas
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rate_limit_config_examples.txt (text)]
